memory_update.text: The pure-play public OPM universe is thin after industry consolidation and stress; private firms such as Risepoint may be better operating benchmarks than investable candidates.
LOPE should remain the primary public-company candidate for outsourced university operating-stack exposure due to explicit services agreements and revenue-share economics with university partners.
COUR should be tracked as an OPM-adjacent platform candidate, especially if degree programs and university partnerships become more material relative to consumer course revenue.
APEI is a speculative shadow candidate, useful for demand read-through into online workforce degree programs but not a direct vendor for the outsourcing node.
Key survival tests for this node are partner enrollment growth, student acquisition cost, retention/completion outcomes, revenue-share regulatory risk, and university partner concentration.
LOPE is the cleanest US-listed direct supplier candidate for online program enablement and university outsourcing because revenue is explicitly tied to services agreements with university partners.
COUR should be tracked as a platform/distribution model for university online degrees and credentials, not as a traditional full-service OPM.
STRA offers a second-order path into online degree demand through employer education-benefit administration and transferable online general-education credits.

Many historically important OPM assets are private, sold, merged, or delisted; later layers should map private reference competitors such as Risepoint/Academic Partnerships and former OPM assets at Pearson/Wiley to benchmark public candidates.
LOPE is the cleanest US-listed direct proxy for outsourced university operating-stack exposure, but later layers must stress-test GCU concentration, regulatory pressure, and partner diversification.
GHC/Kaplan is a hidden OPM/service-provider mapping inside a diversified holding company; the Purdue Global TOSA may be a long-duration customer dependency worth isolating.
COUR is a small-cap platform/distribution proxy for online degrees; degree revenue mix and learner-to-degree conversion are the key evidence gates.

Private OPM leaders such as Risepoint/Academic Partnerships and Boundless Learning appear central to the node but are not US-listed; use them as private-market benchmarks for public candidate comparison rather than as tradable candidates.

The likely chokepoint is not generic LMS software alone but the integrated bundle of compliant student acquisition, enrollment conversion, retention support, course operations, analytics, and university-specific contract execution.
LOPE should remain the primary US-listed reference candidate for the online program enablement node because its filings directly disclose a full-stack university services model.
COUR should be tracked as an underfollowed platform-style exposure to university online degrees and credentials, but degree economics require more verification after the 2025 reporting change.
LRN is an adjacent virtual education operations candidate rather than a higher-ed OPM; include only in second-order screens focused on reusable online learning infrastructure and career pathways.

Many important OPM names are not currently clean US-listed equities: Academic Partnerships/Risepoint is private, Pearson sold its OPM business to Regent, and 2U went through Chapter 11, limiting public-market purity.

Key survival tests for this node are partner enrollment growth, marketing efficiency, student retention, regulatory pressure on revenue-share and third-party-servicer models, and customer concentration.

The cleanest direct public exposure is Grand Canyon Education, which is an education-services provider paid under university partner service agreements. Coursera and Pearson provide platform/OPM-adjacent online learning services to universities, but each has broader business mix. American Public Education is not an outsourced OPM vendor; it is included as a small-cap asset-owner/direct-customer proxy because it operates online postsecondary institutions and workforce-oriented programs that reveal demand for the same enrollment, retention, compliance, and online delivery stack. The key structural caution is that several large private OPMs, such as Risepoint, are not directly investable, and public names may have either customer concentration risk or diluted exposure. Coursera is a platform-style university distribution and online-degree partner rather than a labor-heavy OPM. Strategic Education is a hybrid operator plus second-order employer/university benefits infrastructure through Workforce Edge and Sophia.
